items.title: The Results Are In: Voters Hate Data Centers
items.excerpt: From high-profile Senate races to local rezoning initiatives, data centers and their supporters did miserably on the ballot in the 2026 midterms.

items.title: Data centers lost the midterms
items.excerpt: Three-quarters of voters opposed data centers in their communities in NBC News exit polling.

items.title: Voters deliver "AI earthquake," rebuking tech and billionaires
items.excerpt: Voters approved dozens of data center moratoriums; per Ballotpedia about two dozen of 41 restrict/block measures across 10 states appeared to pass, and Texas governor-elect Hinojosa campaigned on keeping a data center construction moratorium until the legislature acts.

items.title: Big Tech claims voters’ AI backlash is “anti-Trump” not “anti-tech”
items.excerpt: Tech industry in denial as US overwhelmingly votes to restrict AI, data centers.

items.title: Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput.
items.excerpt: Some of the largest AI infrastructure projects in the world are underway in Texas. A dramatic political shift could slow their construction—and deepen concerns about the economics of the AI boom.

items.title: Musk’s Minnesota Deepfake Fight Could Define AI’s First Amendment
items.excerpt: The Eighth Circuit’s review of Minnesota’s strict-liability nudification law may settle what state of mind AI companies need for liability.

items.title: Where the Weight Lies: A Balancing Act for the Governance of Open-Weight AI Models
items.excerpt: What would a ban on open weight models which run artificial intelligence systems actually look like? Could it even be implemented? What implications would it have for the concept of digital sovereignty?

items.title: Metsola tells MEPs not to rely on AI when drafting laws
items.excerpt: European Parliament President Roberta Metsola told MEPs not to rely on AI when drafting laws, as the Parliament prepares guidelines for lawmakers on the use of AI.

items.title: UK Officials Said AI Would Add £400 Billion to the Economy. That Figure Mainly Came From Google
items.excerpt: The AI minister now concedes the estimated figure is less than a third of that. Researchers blame the country’s slow rate of adoption.

items.title: Google Is Forcing AI Overviews in Classrooms. Schools Are Searching for a Way Out
items.excerpt: Google is tying up AI Overviews with traditional search, angering parents and educators who worry that easy, machine-generated answers are leaving kids less capable.

items.title: Google will let schools skip AI tools, but they have to give up search, too
items.excerpt: Google says schools can opt out of its AI tools in education accounts, but doing so also turns off Google Search, since AI Overviews are now built into search.

items.title: Ukraine’s drone strikes spur hasty Russian plans for underground data centers
items.excerpt: After Ukrainian drone strikes on data centers, Russia is drawing up hasty plans to move digital infrastructure, including AI compute, underground.

items.title: AI policy wonks declare 'sovereign agents' a threat to civilization
items.excerpt: These are AI agents that operate outside of human control and 'pursue open-ended, evolving survival'

items.title: Drax wants to feed Britain's AI habit with £20B datacenter at biomass power station
items.excerpt: Drax proposes a £20B AI datacenter at its biomass power station; it first needs planning permission, government approval and a customer.

items.title: Startups recalibrate Chinese AI for the West
items.excerpt: A growing number of startups are editing powerful Chinese open-weight models for Western businesses that are concerned about censorship and security.

items.title: Don’t Let ‘Misaligned’ and ‘Rogue’ Agents Obscure Corporate Accountability in OpenAI–Hugging Face Probes
items.excerpt: Commentary on probes into the OpenAI agent evaluation that breached Hugging Face infrastructure: a reconstructed 64-day timeline argues investigators should examine management decisions, not just 'rogue' model behavior.

items.title: The Incident Report Is Becoming a Building Block of AI Governance
items.excerpt: Dealing with AI harms will be easier if everyone is working from a shared factual record, writes Joseph Hoefer.

items.title: Democratic midterm wins set stage for tougher tech and AI scrutiny | IAPP
items.excerpt: Democratic control of Congress after the 2026 midterms is expected to reshape the US privacy, AI and digital governance agenda, including oversight of federal preemption of state AI laws.

items.title: Deepfakes Are Dominating Global Elections, and Regulation Is Playing Catch-Up
items.excerpt: As AI-generated deepfakes become increasingly prevalent in elections worldwide, governments are struggling to distinguish political expression from deception and enforce regulations before misleading content reaches voters.

items.title: Care workers, women returning to employment and builders to gain practical AI skills
items.excerpt: Four Barnsley training projects will share over £800,000 to bring practical artificial intelligence skills into everyday workplaces.

items.title: Court Bars Meta From Using News Articles to Train AI in Brazil
items.excerpt: A São Paulo court on Nov. 3 barred Meta from using bots to collect news articles, photos and videos from outlets in three Brazilian press associations to train AI; daily fines could reach $182,400.

items.title: EU rules on Artificial Intelligence devices will apply in NI
items.excerpt: The UK government says some EU AI rules, covering AI-integrated products, will apply in Northern Ireland under the Windsor Framework.

items.title: AI chip smugglers exploit trade control loophole to bring banned HBM from South Korea into China — expensive memory chips packaged with cheap, unsanctioned processors to become legal exports
items.excerpt: Smugglers are moving export-controlled HBM from South Korea into China by packaging it with cheap, unsanctioned processors so the bundle ships as a legal export.

items.title: Nvidia tells data center operators to limit business from Chinese customers with new global restrictions, report claims — allegedly restricted to 49% of the total, ensuring 51% are non-Chinese outfits
items.excerpt: Cloud providers have been told that they must sell 51% of their services to non-Chinese companies for the first time.

items.title: Putin demands Russian data centers supply capacity to the state in wake of Ukraine drone attacks — 10% capacity must be available for state IT infrastructure with 24 hours' notice
items.excerpt: Data centers not owned by the Russian state will have 24 hours to provide access to 10% of their capacity if they are called upon.

items.title: Albanese government warned it is ‘sleepwalking into another robodebt scenario’ over use of algorithms and AI
items.excerpt: Centre for Public Integrity report calls for audit and public register of all automated decision-making

items.title: ‘A serious failure’: CPS prosecutor cites imaginary case to court after AI search
items.excerpt: Exclusive: Nonexistent precedent cited in alleged child rape case adds to dozens of AI-related errors plaguing court proceedings

items.title: Medicare’s AI-assisted coverage review pilot hit early snags, documents show
items.excerpt: A top Trump administration official recently acknowledged issues with the program, but the administration has shown no signs of nixing it.
